SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are riddles, proverbs and tongue twisters important? 2. How do we perform riddles, proverbs and tongue twisters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration as a learner uses riddles, tongue twisters and proverbs.

• Critical thinking and problem solving as a learner connects ideas to solve riddles.

Values:
Unity is encouraged as the learners participate in riddling games.

Link to other subjects

French, German, Kiswahili and indigenous languages teach riddles, proverbs and tongue twisters.
